question: Conductors in a feeder have a calculated allowable ampacity of 285 amperes, and no standard overcurrent device rating matches that value. The feeder does not supply multioutlet cord-and-plug circuits. Under Article 240, what overcurrent device rating is permitted for it?

options.A: 250 amperes, the next lower standard size, since protection may only round down
options.B: 350 amperes, the second standard size above, to leave extra room for future load growth
options.C: 300 amperes, the next higher standard size above 285, permitted by 240.4(B) up to 800 amperes
options.D: 285 amperes, since the device may be set to the exact conductor ampacity of the feeder

explanation: The correct answer is C (300 amperes, the next higher standard size above 285, permitted by 240.4(B) up to 800 amperes): Section 240.4(B) permits the next higher standard OCPD rating when the ampacity does not match a standard size, the conductors do not supply multioutlet cord-and-plug circuits, and the next size does not exceed 800 amperes. The standard sizes in 240.6(A) go from 250 to 300 to 350, so 300 amperes is the next above 285. Rounding down is another choice and is not the only option. The 350 ampere answer skips a size.

question: Protecting 10 AWG copper conductors on a circuit, a 20 ampere breaker is installed even though the conductors could carry 30 amperes at 60 degrees C. According to Article 210, which characteristic classifies this circuit as a 20 ampere branch circuit?

options.A: The ampacity of the conductors, which is 30 amperes at the 60 degree column
options.B: The connected load in volt-amperes, which determines the correct circuit class in every case
options.C: The rating of the receptacles installed on the circuit, which sets the circuit class by default
options.D: The rating of the overcurrent device protecting the circuit

explanation: The correct answer is D (The rating of the overcurrent device protecting the circuit): Section 210.3 classifies branch circuits by the maximum permitted rating or setting of the overcurrent device that protects them. With a 20 ampere breaker, the circuit is a 20 ampere branch circuit regardless of what the conductors could carry. Conductor ampacity and connected load are design inputs but do not set the classification. Receptacle ratings are limited by the circuit rating, not the reverse.

question: Inspecting a new feeder that uses two parallel sets of 250 kcmil copper conductors per phase in separate raceways, an inspector checks the sets against Article 310. The installer has left the conductor tags attached for review. Which condition must the parallel sets meet?

options.A: Each set matches in length, material, size, insulation type, and terminations
options.B: The sets may differ in length if total resistance is balanced by a larger conductor size
options.C: The sets may differ in size if bundled together in one raceway for part of it
options.D: The sets must match in length and size, but their insulation types are allowed to differ

explanation: The correct answer is A (Each set matches in length, material, size, insulation type, and terminations): Section 310.10(G) requires parallel conductors to have the same length, conductor material, size in circular mil area, and insulation type, and to be terminated the same way. Matching characteristics ensure the sets share current equally. Different lengths or sizes cause unequal current sharing even if total resistance seems balanced. Insulation type must also match, since different types change the conductor impedance and ampacity.

question: Boring holes through the center of 2x6 wood studs for NM cable, an apprentice leaves only 19 mm of wood between each hole edge and the nearest stud edge. The cable will run horizontally through several studs in an exterior wall. What does Article 300 require for these cable holes?

options.A: At least 19 mm of wood is enough, since the cable is nonmetallic and unarmored
options.B: At least 32 mm, or 1 1/4 inches, of wood or a steel plate
options.C: At least 50 mm, or 2 inches, of wood must remain at every hole bored
options.D: At least 13 mm of wood is enough when the cable is fastened beside each hole

explanation: The correct answer is B (At least 32 mm, or 1 1/4 inches, of wood or a steel plate): Section 300.4(A)(1) requires the hole edge to be at least 1 1/4 inches (32 mm) from the nearest edge of the wood framing member. Otherwise the cable needs a listed steel plate at least 1/16 inch thick covering the area. With only 19 mm remaining, a nail or screw could reach the cable, so the installation fails. The 19 mm figure is tempting but falls below the required distance.

question: Planning a long straight run of rigid metal conduit through a mechanical shaft, a crew needs support spacing under Article 344 and its general rule. What is the maximum spacing between supports, with the first support placed near each enclosure?

options.A: 4.5 feet between supports, the interval that applies to liquidtight flexible metal conduit in general
options.B: 10 feet between supports, with one within 3 feet of each enclosure, per Section 344.30
options.C: 12 feet between supports, with one placed within 6 feet of each enclosure at the ends
options.D: 3 feet between supports, with one placed within 1 foot of each enclosure at the ends

explanation: The correct answer is B (10 feet between supports, with one within 3 feet of each enclosure, per Section 344.30): Section 344.30 requires rigid metal conduit to be supported within 3 feet of each outlet box, junction box, device box, cabinet, or fitting, and then at intervals not exceeding 10 feet under the general rule. Liquidtight flexible metal conduit has a shorter interval of 4.5 feet, which is the tempting wrong choice. The 12 foot option also pairs its spacing with a 6 foot distance from each enclosure, which exceeds the 3 foot limit. Short spacing of 3 feet may apply to some nonmetallic conduit sizes but is not what rigid metal requires.

question: Across a lawn, a 120 volt, 20 ampere GFCI-protected residential branch circuit will run in direct-burial Type UF cable to a detached shed at a one-family dwelling. The shed holds only lighting and two receptacles for hand tools. Which minimum cover applies under Table 300.5?

options.A: 12 inches, since GFCI protection and 20 ampere overcurrent protection allow reduced residential cover
options.B: 24 inches, the general cover for directly buried cable without any residential reduction applied
options.C: 18 inches, the cover for PVC conduit placed in the same trench as the cable run
options.D: 6 inches, the cover permitted for rigid metal conduit placed in the same trench

explanation: The correct answer is A (12 inches, since GFCI protection and 20 ampere overcurrent protection allow reduced residential cover): Table 300.5 gives a reduced cover column for residential branch circuits rated 120 volts or less, protected by a GFCI and with overcurrent protection of 20 amperes or less. UF cable here qualifies for 12 inches. The 24 inch value is for ordinary direct buried cable, 18 inches is for PVC conduit, and 6 inches is for rigid metal conduit. Each belongs to a different column of the table.

question: Found with no intermediate supports between two boxes, a 7.2 meter horizontal run of Type MC cable failed rough-in inspection. Supports are required within 300 mm of each box and at intervals not over 1.8 m. What is the minimum number of supports for the run?

options.A: Five supports, with the end ones within 300 mm of boxes
options.B: Three supports, dividing the run into four equal 1.8 meter spans from box to box
options.C: Four supports, counting 1.8 meter spans after the first box support only along the run
options.D: Two supports, spacing them at 2.4 meter intervals along the horizontal run between the two boxes

explanation: The correct answer is A (Five supports, with the end ones within 300 mm of boxes): Section 330.30 requires MC cable supports within 300 mm of each box and at no more than 1.8 m between supports. The span between the first and last supports is 7.2 minus 0.6, or 6.6 m, and 6.6 divided by 1.8 gives 3.67, so four spans are required. Four spans need five supports. Counting only intermediate supports yields three, which leaves the terminal ends unsupported.

question: Supplying a 30 ampere load, a tap from a feeder protected at 400 amperes is made with the 10 foot tap rule, and the tap conductors are enclosed in a raceway. Based only on the feeder overcurrent rating, what minimum tap ampacity does the 10 foot rule require?

options.A: At least 133 amperes, one third of the feeder rating, from the 25 foot rule
options.B: At least 100 amperes, one quarter of the feeder overcurrent device rating in this tap rule
options.C: At least 30 amperes, matching the connected load with no ratio to the feeder device rating
options.D: At least 40 amperes, one tenth of the 400 ampere feeder device rating under Section 240.21(B)(1)

explanation: The correct answer is D (At least 40 amperes, one tenth of the 400 ampere feeder device rating under Section 240.21(B)(1)): Section 240.21(B)(1) allows a 10 foot tap if the tap ampacity is not less than the calculated loads and not less than the rating of the device it supplies, and if the tap ampacity is at least one tenth of the feeder overcurrent rating. One tenth of 400 amperes is 40 amperes, which exceeds the 30 ampere load. The one third value belongs to the 25 foot tap rule, which has additional conditions. Using the load alone ignores the ratio test.

question: Feeding a detached garage from the main dwelling panel with a four-wire feeder, an electrician bonds the grounded conductor to the equipment grounding bus inside the garage panelboard. The feeder also carries a green equipment grounding conductor from the main panel. What does Article 250 require at this garage panel?

options.A: The bond is required at every building disconnect, including the panelboard in the detached garage
options.B: The neutral and equipment grounding conductors stay separate, with no bond at the garage panel
options.C: The bond is allowed if the garage has its own grounding electrode installed at the building
options.D: The bond is required when the feeder to the second building is rated 100 amperes

explanation: The correct answer is B (The neutral and equipment grounding conductors stay separate, with no bond at the garage panel): For a separate building fed by a feeder with an equipment grounding conductor, 250.32(B) requires the grounded conductor to be isolated from the equipment grounding conductor and enclosures at the second building. Bonding them there creates parallel return paths on the grounding system. The neutral-to-ground bond belongs only at the service or a separately derived system. A local electrode does not change this.

question: Sizing the disconnecting means for a motor with a full-load current of 90 amperes under Article 430, an electrician applies the ampere rule in 430.110(A). The motor is a standard continuous duty unit driving a pump. What minimum ampere rating does that rule require for the disconnect?

options.A: 103.5 amperes, which is 115 percent of the full-load current
options.B: 112.5 amperes, which is 125 percent of the full-load current for continuous duty operation
options.C: 90.0 amperes, which equals the full-load current with no added percentage factor applied
options.D: 135.0 amperes, which is 150 percent of the full-load current to allow for the starting

explanation: The correct answer is A (103.5 amperes, which is 115 percent of the full-load current): Section 430.110(A) requires the ampere rating of the disconnecting means to be at least 115 percent of the motor full-load current. Multiplying 90 by 1.15 gives 103.5 amperes. The 125 percent factor is used for motor conductors and for continuous loads and does not apply to this disconnect. Starting current does not enter the disconnect ampere rating rule.

question: Qualifying under the 25 foot tap rule, a tap is run from a 400 ampere feeder overcurrent device to a 120 ampere load, with terminations rated 75 degrees C. All tap conditions other than conductor size have already been checked and met. What is the smallest copper tap conductor allowed?

options.A: 1 AWG, using its 130 ampere rating as satisfying one third of the 400 ampere rating
options.B: 1/0 AWG, since one third of 400 is 133.3 amperes and 1 AWG carries 130
options.C: 3/0 AWG, using one half of 400 amperes, or 200 amperes, as the target tap ampacity
options.D: 8 AWG, using one tenth of 400 amperes, or 40 amperes, from the 10 foot rule

explanation: The correct answer is B (1/0 AWG, since one third of 400 is 133.3 amperes and 1 AWG carries 130): Section 240.21(B)(2) requires 25 foot tap conductors to have ampacity of at least one third of the feeder overcurrent device rating. One third of 400 is 133.3 amperes. In the 75 degree column of Table 310.16, 1 AWG carries 130 amperes, which falls just under, while 1/0 AWG carries 150 amperes, which satisfies the rule and the 120 ampere load. Rounding 133.3 down to 130 is the tempting error.

question: Before applying any other factor to size conductors for a three-phase 208 volt heating bank nameplated at 18 kilovolt-amperes, the electrician first needs the load current. The three phase supply is fed by a 208 volt, four wire wye service. What is the line current of this bank in amperes?

options.A: 86.5 amperes, using 18,000 divided by 208 volts as for a single-phase load on the bank
options.B: 28.8 amperes, using 18,000 divided by 3 times 208 volts instead of root three times 208
options.C: 75.0 amperes, using 18,000 divided by 240 volts as for a single-phase load on the circuit
options.D: 50.0 amperes, using 18,000 divided by root three times 208 volts for one three-phase line

explanation: The correct answer is D (50.0 amperes, using 18,000 divided by root three times 208 volts for one three-phase line): Three-phase line current equals volt-amperes divided by the square root of three times the line voltage. The square root of three is 1.732, so 1.732 times 208 equals 360.3. Dividing 18,000 by 360.3 gives 50.0 amperes. Using the single-phase formula gives 86.5 amperes and overstates the current by about 1.73 times.

question: In a small shop, a 4,500 watt storage water heater at 240 volts is treated as a continuous load. The electrician finds the load current and then applies the continuous load factor. What minimum branch circuit rating, in amperes, results?

options.A: 18.8 amperes, which is the load current with no continuous load factor applied to the heater
options.B: 23.4 amperes, which is 125 percent of 18.75 amperes, the 4,500-watt heater current at 240 volts
options.C: 29.3 amperes, which applies the 125 percent factor twice to the load current of the heater
options.D: 20.6 amperes, which is 110 percent of the load current of 18.75 amperes for the heater

explanation: The correct answer is B (23.4 amperes, which is 125 percent of 18.75 amperes, the 4,500-watt heater current at 240 volts): Load current is 4,500 divided by 240, or 18.75 amperes. Storage water heaters are treated as continuous loads here, so 18.75 times 1.25 equals 23.4 amperes minimum branch-circuit rating. Skipping the factor gives 18.8 amperes. Applying 125 percent twice gives 29.3 amperes, which overstates the requirement.

question: Above the stage of a school auditorium, a touring production hangs temporary stage lighting on a portable truss, with portable stage switchboards supplying dimmers. The district has adopted the 2026 NEC and the fire marshal plans an inspection. Which article of the NEC contains the specific rules for this stage lighting and equipment?

options.A: Article 525, which covers carnivals, circuses, fairs, and similar traveling attractions that move
options.B: Article 518, which covers all wiring of assembly occupancies including every kind of stage equipment
options.C: Article 520, covering theaters and similar places with stage lighting and portable stage switchboards
options.D: Article 530, which covers motion picture and television studios and other similar production locations

explanation: The correct answer is C (Article 520, covering theaters and similar places with stage lighting and portable stage switchboards): Article 520 contains the specific requirements for theaters, audience areas of motion picture and television studios, and places of assembly with stage lighting, including portable switchboards and stage lighting. Article 518 covers assembly occupancies in general but leaves stage equipment to Article 520. Article 525 addresses carnivals and fairs, and Article 530 addresses film and television studios, so neither fits a school auditorium stage.

question: Supplying several general-purpose receptacle outlets in an office, a 20 ampere branch circuit uses 12 AWG conductors. The building owner asks about the largest receptacle rating the design may use. Under the Article 210 table for receptacle ratings on multioutlet circuits, which receptacle ratings are permitted on it?

options.A: Only 20 ampere rated receptacles, since the receptacle rating must match the circuit rating exactly
options.B: Only 15 ampere rated receptacles, since they are the most common type installed in offices
options.C: Receptacles up to 30 amperes, since 10 AWG conductors could carry that much current safely
options.D: Either 15 ampere or 20 ampere rated receptacles

explanation: The correct answer is D (Either 15 ampere or 20 ampere rated receptacles): Section 210.21(B)(3) permits either 15 or 20 ampere receptacles on a 20 ampere circuit that supplies two or more receptacle outlets. A 15 ampere receptacle is not prohibited there. Receptacle ratings are tied to the circuit rating, not the conductor ampacity, so a 30 ampere receptacle would be too large. Requiring only the circuit rating ignores the table.

question: Sized for a new service panel, the loads include 280 amperes of continuous load and 60 amperes of noncontinuous load. The service voltage is 208 volts and the panel will be fed with copper conductors. Using standard overcurrent device sizes, what is the minimum overcurrent device rating required for the service?

options.A: 350 amperes, found by rounding up the plain 340 ampere sum
options.B: 400 amperes, found by rounding the 410 ampere result down to the nearest standard size
options.C: 450 amperes, since the 410 ampere calculated load rounds up to the next standard size
options.D: 600 amperes, found by applying 125 percent twice to the 340 ampere total

explanation: The correct answer is C (450 amperes, since the 410 ampere calculated load rounds up to the next standard size): The device must carry 125 percent of the continuous load plus 100 percent of the noncontinuous load: 280 times 1.25 equals 350, plus 60 gives 410 amperes. The standard sizes in this range are 400 and 450, and 400 is below 410, so 450 amperes is the minimum. Using the plain 340 ampere sum skips the continuous factor. Rounding down to 400 leaves the device undersized.

question: Exposed on an outdoor wall of a loading dock with no roof or overhang, a receptacle marked for damp locations only was installed. The wall faces the weather and rain reaches it directly during storms. Under Article 406, what is required for the receptacle at this location?

options.A: A gasketed cover plate, since a damp rating is enough outdoors once a gasket is added
options.B: A GFCI receptacle, since GFCI protection removes the need for any special cover or enclosure
options.C: A flip-lid cover that stays weatherproof only when the lid is closed over the receptacle face
options.D: An enclosure weatherproof with a plug inserted, an extra-duty in-use cover, for wet locations

explanation: The correct answer is D (An enclosure weatherproof with a plug inserted, an extra-duty in-use cover, for wet locations): A fully exposed outdoor wall with no roof is a wet location. Section 406.9(B) requires receptacles there, 15 and 20 ampere at 125 and 250 volts, to be in an enclosure that is weatherproof whether or not a plug is inserted, an in-use cover listed as extra-duty. A damp location rating is not enough, and a simple lid cover fails once a cord is plugged in. GFCI protection is separate from the enclosure requirement.

question: Settling on equipment surfaces, combustible dust at a grain processing plant becomes airborne in ignitable amounts only during abnormal operation, such as an equipment malfunction. The plant manager supplied a hazardous area drawing but left the classification blank. How should this location be classified under Article 500?

options.A: Class II, Division 1, since grain dust is present every time the plant operates
options.B: Class II, Division 2, since combustible dust is not normally suspended in ignitable concentrations
options.C: Class III, Division 1, since grain dust behaves as an easily ignitable fiber or flying material
options.D: Class I, Division 2, since flammable vapors form during abnormal operation at grain processing plants

explanation: The correct answer is B (Class II, Division 2, since combustible dust is not normally suspended in ignitable concentrations): Combustible dust locations fall in Class II. Division 1 applies where dust is normally suspended in ignitable quantities or where equipment failure could make it so while also causing an ignition source. Division 2 applies where dust is not normally suspended and accumulations are not normally enough to interfere with equipment, as here. Class III is for easily ignitable fibers and Class I is for flammable gases and vapors, neither of which describes grain dust.

question: Offered by an equipment supplier, a motor is listed and marked for Class I, Division 2 locations, yet the purchaser plans to install it in a Class I, Division 1 location at a solvent plant. What is the Code position on this motor?

options.A: It is suitable, since a Division 2 listing covers both Division 1 and Division 2 areas
options.B: It is suitable if a conduit seal fitting is added within 18 inches of the motor
options.C: It is not suitable, since a Division 1 location requires equipment identified for Division 1
options.D: It is suitable if the motor is totally enclosed and fan cooled, whatever its listing

explanation: The correct answer is C (It is not suitable, since a Division 1 location requires equipment identified for Division 1): Equipment identified for Division 1 can be used in Division 2, but the reverse is not true. A Division 2 listing means the equipment is acceptable only where ignitable concentrations are not normally present. A Division 1 location needs equipment listed for Division 1 or a protection method suitable for it. Adding a seal or choosing a totally enclosed motor does not convert the identification.

question: Nameplate data on a 15 horsepower, 460 volt, three-phase motor show a full-load current of 19.5 amperes, while Table 430.250 lists 21 amperes for that rating. The branch circuit is fed from a 480 volt panelboard and uses copper conductors. Which current value sizes the branch circuit conductors for this motor?

options.A: The 19.5 ampere nameplate value, since it reflects the actual motor installed on this circuit
options.B: The 19.5 ampere nameplate for conductors, and the 21 ampere table value for the overloads
options.C: The 21 ampere value from Table 430.250, since conductor sizing uses the table, not the nameplate
options.D: The 24.4 ampere value, which is 125 percent of the nameplate current rating of the motor

explanation: The correct answer is C (The 21 ampere value from Table 430.250, since conductor sizing uses the table, not the nameplate): Section 430.6(A)(1) requires the table full-load current, not the nameplate, for sizing conductors, disconnects, and short-circuit protection. Nameplate current is used for overload protection under 430.6(A)(2). The conductor minimum is then 125 percent of 21 amperes, which is 26.25 amperes. Using the nameplate for conductors, or swapping the two roles, is the common mix-up.

question: Carrying 80 amperes of noncontinuous load and 150 amperes of continuous load, a feeder must be protected under 215.3. The feeder serves a panelboard in a small manufacturing building with copper conductors. What minimum standard rating of overcurrent device should protect this feeder?

options.A: 250 amperes, from applying 125 percent only to the 80 ampere noncontinuous load portion
options.B: 300 amperes, since 267.5 amperes calculated rounds up to the next standard size in 240.6(A)
options.C: 225 amperes, from rounding down the plain 230 ampere sum of the continuous and other loads
options.D: 350 amperes, from applying 125 percent twice to the 150 ampere continuous load of the feeder

explanation: The correct answer is B (300 amperes, since 267.5 amperes calculated rounds up to the next standard size in 240.6(A)): Section 215.3 requires the device rating to be at least the noncontinuous load plus 125 percent of the continuous load. That is 80 plus 187.5, or 267.5 amperes. The next standard size above 267.5 is 300 amperes. Applying the factor to the noncontinuous load gives 250 amperes, which is below the requirement. Applying it twice gives 350 amperes, which is larger than needed.

question: Buried under a landscaped lawn at a commercial building, a 480 volt feeder in rigid metal conduit has no special reduction conditions. The conduit is a metal raceway with no concrete encasement or other special condition. What minimum cover does Table 300.5 require for rigid metal conduit in this case?

options.A: 12 inches, the reduced cover for GFCI protected residential branch circuits at 120 volts or less
options.B: 18 inches, the cover listed for nonmetallic raceways listed for direct burial in the table
options.C: 24 inches, the cover listed for directly buried cable installed without any raceway around it
options.D: 6 inches, the cover listed for rigid metal conduit

explanation: The correct answer is D (6 inches, the cover listed for rigid metal conduit): Table 300.5 gives 6 inches of minimum cover for rigid metal conduit and intermediate metal conduit in the general case. Direct buried cables need 24 inches and listed nonmetallic raceways need 18 inches. The 12 inch value applies only to residential 120 volt, 20 ampere GFCI protected branch circuits, which a 480 volt commercial feeder is not.

question: Wiring a general care patient bed location in a hospital, an electrician consults Article 517 for receptacle requirements. The project covers a new wing with several general care patient rooms. Which description of the receptacle requirement for each such bed location is correct?

options.A: At least four hospital-grade receptacles on a single normal-system branch circuit for each bed
options.B: At least two hospital-grade receptacles on two separate branch circuits for each bed location
options.C: At least four hospital-grade receptacles on two separate branch circuits
options.D: At least fourteen hospital-grade receptacles on two separate branch circuits for each bed location

explanation: The correct answer is C (At least four hospital-grade receptacles on two separate branch circuits): For general care areas, 517.18 requires at least two branch circuits at each patient bed location, one from the emergency system and one from the normal system, and a minimum of four receptacle outlets listed as hospital grade. A single circuit leaves the bed without the second source, and only two receptacles falls short of the count. Fourteen receptacles is the larger minimum for critical care locations, which is a different space category.

question: Leaving a feeder outdoors, tap conductors run 40 feet along the exterior wall of a warehouse before entering the building through the wall, protected from physical damage. The tap conductors are copper and are sized to match the load they will serve. Which Article 240 tap rule can allow this length?

options.A: The 10 foot tap rule, which applies once the conductors enter the building through the wall
options.B: The outside feeder tap rule, with conductors ending at a single overcurrent protective device at entrance
options.C: The 25 foot tap rule, which allows 25 feet inside or outside the building as needed
options.D: The transformer secondary tap rule, which allows unlimited length with no protective device needed

explanation: The correct answer is B (The outside feeder tap rule, with conductors ending at a single overcurrent protective device at entrance): The outside feeder tap rule in 240.21(B) permits taps of unlimited length if the conductors are outdoors except at the load termination, are protected from physical damage, and end at a single circuit breaker or set of fuses sized for the tap ampacity, located at the nearest point of entrance as part of the building disconnect. The 10 and 25 foot rules have fixed length limits that 40 feet exceeds.

question: Running from a weatherproof box to a rooftop condensing unit, a 13 foot liquidtight flexible metal conduit whip carries only the circuit conductors, with no separate grounding wire. The whip is the only wiring method between the box and the unit disconnect. Under Article 350, what does the inspector require?

options.A: Nothing further, because listed fittings let the conduit serve as the grounding path at any length
options.B: A separate equipment grounding conductor, since 13 feet exceeds the 6 foot limit for conduit grounding
options.C: Nothing further, because three quarter inch conduit is large enough to serve as the grounding path
options.D: Replacement with EMT, because liquidtight flexible conduit is limited to 6 feet in overall length

explanation: The correct answer is B (A separate equipment grounding conductor, since 13 feet exceeds the 6 foot limit for conduit grounding): Section 350.60 allows liquidtight flexible metal conduit to serve as the equipment grounding conductor only in short lengths of 6 feet or less, with listed fittings and limited overcurrent protection. A 13 foot whip exceeds that, so a wire-type equipment grounding conductor is required. The conduit itself is not limited to 6 feet in length, only its use as the grounding path.

question: Testing rapid shutdown on a commercial rooftop PV system, an inspector initiates shutdown and, after 30 seconds, reads 60 volts on controlled conductors beyond the array boundary. The system uses module level devices and the array boundary is one foot from the modules. How should this result be judged under Article 690?

options.A: Compliant, since an 80 volt limit applies to every conductor of the system at 30 seconds
options.B: Compliant, since 60 volts is below the 120 volt level of normal building circuits in service
options.C: Noncompliant, since 30 volts or less is required within 30 seconds outside the array boundary
options.D: Noncompliant, since conductors must fall to 15 volts or less within 10 seconds of initiation

explanation: The correct answer is C (Noncompliant, since 30 volts or less is required within 30 seconds outside the array boundary): Section 690.12 requires controlled conductors outside the array boundary to reduce to 30 volts or less within 30 seconds of shutdown initiation. Inside the array boundary the limit is 80 volts within 30 seconds. Because the measured conductors are beyond the boundary, 60 volts exceeds the 30 volt limit and the system fails the test. The 15 volt and 10 second values are not part of the rule.

question: Planning floor receptacles in a warehouse slab, an electrician intends to cast Type UF cable directly into the poured concrete with no conduit around it. The slab will be poured over a vapor barrier and gravel base next week. What does Article 340 say about this installation?

options.A: It is permitted, since the moisture resistant jacket of UF cable suits contact with wet concrete
options.B: It is permitted when a 2 inch layer of sand surrounds the cable before the pour
options.C: It is permitted only for lighting circuits not exceeding 15 amperes in the slab
options.D: It is not permitted, since UF cable cannot be embedded in poured concrete, cement or aggregate

explanation: The correct answer is D (It is not permitted, since UF cable cannot be embedded in poured concrete, cement or aggregate): Section 340.12 lists uses not permitted for Type UF cable, including embedding in poured cement, concrete, or aggregate. The moisture resistant jacket is meant for burial in earth and wet locations, not for casting in a slab. Placing the cable in a listed raceway suitable for embedding would be the correct approach. Neither a sand layer nor a lower circuit rating creates an exception.

question: Supplying a floating building from a shore panel at a marina, a feeder is being installed under Article 553. The marina owner wants the feeder routed along the pier to the shore panel. What must this feeder include along with its circuit conductors?

options.A: A bare equipment grounding conductor in a separate raceway buried beside the feeder cable run
options.B: A grounded conductor bonded to the floating building enclosure at its main panel on the dock
options.C: A bonding jumper to the shore piping system instead of any equipment grounding conductor
options.D: An insulated equipment grounding conductor run with the feeder conductors in the same raceway

explanation: The correct answer is D (An insulated equipment grounding conductor run with the feeder conductors in the same raceway): Article 553 requires the feeder to a floating building to include an insulated equipment grounding conductor with the circuit conductors, so fault current has a return path to the supply. The grounded conductor must not be bonded to enclosures at the floating building, and shore piping is not a substitute for the conductor. A bare conductor run separately does not match the wiring method rules for the feeder.

question: At a parking garage, the owner adds a ceiling-mounted EV charger that the manufacturer rates at 32 amperes and that will charge fleet vehicles overnight for many hours. The installer is sizing the dedicated branch circuit for this continuous load. What is the minimum branch-circuit rating the installer must use?

options.A: 40 amperes, found by multiplying the load current by 125 percent
options.B: 32 amperes, using the nameplate rating with no continuous-load factor applied
options.C: 50 amperes, applying the 125 percent factor twice to the nameplate rating
options.D: 35 amperes, using a 110 percent factor on the nameplate rating

explanation: The correct answer is A (40 amperes, found by multiplying the load current by 125 percent): Article 625 treats EVSE as a continuous load, so the branch circuit must be rated at 125 percent of 32 amperes, which is 40 amperes. The 32 ampere answer skips the factor. The 50 ampere answer multiplies by 1.25 twice (32 x 1.25 x 1.25 = 50).

question: Reviewing a school addition, a plan reviewer asks which conductors count as feeders under the Article 100 definition. The drawings show the utility transformer connected to a main switchboard, conduit running from that switchboard to a lighting panelboard, and cables from the panelboard breakers out to classroom receptacles. Which conductors are feeders?

options.A: Conductors between the service equipment and the final branch-circuit overcurrent device
options.B: Conductors from each panelboard breaker out to the classroom receptacle outlets
options.C: Conductors from the utility transformer terminals to the main switchboard disconnect
options.D: Every conductor downstream of the utility transformer, including those serving receptacle outlets

explanation: The correct answer is A (Conductors between the service equipment and the final branch-circuit overcurrent device): Article 100 defines a feeder as all circuit conductors between the service equipment, source of a separately derived system, or other power supply source and the final branch-circuit overcurrent device. The conduit run to the lighting panelboard fits that definition. The cables to the receptacles are branch-circuit conductors, and the transformer conductors are service conductors.

question: Each module in a residential PV string lists a short-circuit current of 10 amperes, and the string runs through conduit to a combiner on a detached garage roof. The installer must find the minimum conductor ampacity for the source circuit before any temperature correction or adjustment. The array has twelve modules. What is that minimum ampacity?

options.A: 10.0 amperes, taking the short-circuit current without any multiplier
options.B: 12.5 amperes, applying 125 percent only once to the short-circuit current
options.C: 15.6 amperes, applying 125 percent twice to the short-circuit current
options.D: 19.5 amperes, applying 125 percent three times to the short-circuit current

explanation: The correct answer is C (15.6 amperes, applying 125 percent twice to the short-circuit current): Maximum circuit current for a PV source circuit is 125 percent of the short-circuit current, which is 12.5 amperes. Conductors must carry 125 percent of that value because the load is continuous, so 12.5 x 1.25 = 15.6 amperes. The module count and distance do not change this calculation.

question: Failing a detached garage, an inspector notes a single 20 ampere circuit feeding one receptacle for a shop air compressor. The installer used a 15 ampere receptacle because the compressor draws only 11 amperes, and the cord is rated for 15 amperes. What correction does the inspector require?

options.A: Accept the 15 ampere receptacle because a duplex receptacle on a 20 ampere circuit is permitted
options.B: Install a 30 ampere receptacle so its rating exceeds the circuit rating
options.C: Install a 20 ampere receptacle, since a lone receptacle must match the circuit rating
options.D: Accept the 15 ampere receptacle when the circuit is also GFCI protected

explanation: The correct answer is C (Install a 20 ampere receptacle, since a lone receptacle must match the circuit rating): A single receptacle on an individual branch circuit must have an ampere rating not less than that of the circuit. The compressor load of 11 amperes and the cord rating do not change that. The 15 ampere allowance applies only where two or more receptacles share a 20 ampere circuit.

question: Equipment terminals with no temperature marking will carry a nonmotor 50 ampere load that is not continuous. The electrician has THHN copper conductors on the truck and must pick the smallest size that satisfies the termination temperature rule. Which choice is the smallest conductor that works?

options.A: 8 AWG THHN, using its 75 degree Celsius column of 50 amperes
options.B: 6 AWG THHN, using its 60 degree Celsius column of 55 amperes
options.C: 8 AWG THHN, using its 90 degree Celsius column of 55 amperes
options.D: 10 AWG THHN, using its 90 degree Celsius column of 40 amperes

explanation: The correct answer is B (6 AWG THHN, using its 60 degree Celsius column of 55 amperes): Where equipment terminals for circuits of 100 amperes or less are unmarked, the 60 degree Celsius column of Table 310.16 governs. The 60 degree column gives 40 amperes for 8 AWG, which is too small, and 55 amperes for 6 AWG, which carries 50 amperes. The 75 and 90 degree columns apply only when terminals are marked for those temperatures.

question: A 3,200 square foot house has a calculated load of 195 amperes at 240 volts after all Article 120 demand factors, and the owner has a 400 ampere meter socket on order. The electrician must choose the minimum standard rating for the service disconnect. Which rating is the minimum?

options.A: 200 amperes, the standard size that carries the calculated load
options.B: 250 amperes, found by taking 125 percent of the calculated load
options.C: 100 amperes, the smallest rating allowed for any one-family dwelling service
options.D: 225 amperes, stepping up one size above 200 for extra headroom

explanation: The correct answer is A (200 amperes, the standard size that carries the calculated load): The demand-factor load of 195 amperes already reflects the expected service load, so the disconnect must be at least 195 amperes, and the next standard rating is 200 amperes. The 100 ampere minimum is a floor, not the answer for this load. Applying 125 percent would be correct only for continuous loads that were not already part of a demand calculation.

question: On a residential lot, a utility representative reviews a new 120/240 volt service drop for a ranch house. The drop crosses the family driveway where cars and pickup trucks park, with no commercial truck traffic. The electrician must confirm the minimum vertical clearance at the lowest point of the drop. What clearance applies?

options.A: 10 feet above the driveway, the clearance at the building entrance
options.B: 12 feet above the driveway, the residential value
options.C: 15 feet above the driveway, the value for higher voltage to ground
options.D: 18 feet above the driveway, the value for truck-traffic areas

explanation: The correct answer is B (12 feet above the driveway, the residential value): For service drops of 300 volts or less to ground, 230.24(B) requires 12 feet above residential property and driveways not subject to truck traffic. Ten feet applies only at the building and the drip loop. Eighteen feet applies over streets, alleys and areas subject to truck traffic.

question: Nameplate data on a motor lists a full-load current of 88 amperes and a marked service factor of 1.15. The electrician is selecting separate overload relays and must set the maximum trip rating according to the motor rules. What percentage of the nameplate current is the maximum trip setting?

options.A: 125 percent of nameplate current, matching the marked service factor of 1.15
options.B: 115 percent of the nameplate full-load current, for motors lacking a service factor
options.C: 140 percent of the nameplate full-load current, for trips during motor starting
options.D: 100 percent of the nameplate full-load current, with no allowance added

explanation: The correct answer is A (125 percent of nameplate current, matching the marked service factor of 1.15): For a motor marked with a service factor of 1.15 or more, the overload device may be selected or set at no more than 125 percent of the nameplate current. The 115 percent figure applies to motors without that marking. The 140 percent figure is an upper limit allowed only if the lower setting would not carry the motor through starting.

question: In a factory, an inspector rejects a 20 inch long pull box. A single 3 inch conduit enters one end and a single 3 inch conduit leaves the opposite end in a straight line, carrying conductors of 4 AWG and larger. The contractor asks for the minimum box length that would pass. What length is required?

options.A: 18 inches, six times the trade size of the conduit
options.B: 24 inches, eight times the trade size of the conduit
options.C: 30 inches, ten times the trade size of the conduit
options.D: 36 inches, twelve times the trade size of the conduit

explanation: The correct answer is B (24 inches, eight times the trade size of the conduit): A straight pull with conductors of 4 AWG or larger requires a box at least eight times the trade size of the largest raceway, which is 8 x 3 = 24 inches. The six times multiplier belongs to angle pulls, and it is also paired with the sum of other raceways. The existing 20 inch box fails.

question: Using 6 AWG copper, an installer connected the grounding electrode conductor for a service with 4/0 AWG copper ungrounded conductors, and the inspector objects. The conductor goes to the metal underground water pipe and building steel. Using the grounding electrode conductor table, what is the minimum copper size?

options.A: 2 AWG copper, the row for service conductors over 3/0 AWG through 350 kcmil
options.B: 4 AWG copper, the row for service conductors of 2/0 AWG and 3/0 AWG
options.C: 6 AWG copper, the row for service conductors of 1 AWG and 1/0 AWG
options.D: 1/0 AWG copper, the row for service conductors over 350 kcmil through 600 kcmil

explanation: The correct answer is A (2 AWG copper, the row for service conductors over 3/0 AWG through 350 kcmil): Table 250.66 sizes the grounding electrode conductor from the largest ungrounded service conductor. A 4/0 AWG copper conductor falls in the over 3/0 through 350 kcmil row, which requires 2 AWG copper. The 6 AWG limit applies only when the conductor goes solely to a ground rod, and that does not describe this installation.

question: While wiring a new house kitchen, a contractor plans the receptacles that serve the countertop, pantry and breakfast room. She asks the inspector what the minimum number of small-appliance branch circuits is for these areas. Which statement gives the correct minimum?

options.A: One 20 ampere circuit shared by the countertop receptacles and the kitchen lighting
options.B: Two 20 ampere circuits serving only the kitchen, pantry, breakfast and dining areas
options.C: Two 15 ampere circuits serving the countertop, pantry and breakfast room
options.D: Three 20 ampere circuits, one each for the countertop, pantry and breakfast room

explanation: The correct answer is B (Two 20 ampere circuits serving only the kitchen, pantry, breakfast and dining areas): A dwelling needs at least two 20 ampere small-appliance branch circuits for receptacles in the kitchen, pantry, breakfast room and dining room. These circuits supply no other outlets, so the kitchen lighting cannot share them. A requirement of three circuits is not in the code.

question: Bedroom wiring in a new house uses a 120 volt, 15 ampere circuit that feeds lighting outlets, a smoke alarm and several receptacles. The inspector asks which protection the code requires for the whole branch circuit in this location, and the contractor must answer correctly before the walls are closed. Which protection applies?

options.A: Ground-fault circuit-interrupter protection covering the entire bedroom branch circuit
options.B: Combination-type arc-fault interrupter protection on the full bedroom branch circuit, per Article 210
options.C: A surge protective device installed at the panelboard and listed for branch circuits
options.D: Ground-fault protection of equipment installed in the branch-circuit breaker enclosure

explanation: The correct answer is B (Combination-type arc-fault interrupter protection on the full bedroom branch circuit, per Article 210): Branch circuits of 120 volts, 15 and 20 amperes that supply outlets in dwelling unit bedrooms need arc-fault circuit-interrupter protection, and a combination-type device is the standard way to provide it. GFCI protection applies to other locations such as bathrooms, garages and outdoors, not to bedrooms. The code expects arc-fault protection in these habitable rooms because arcing faults in cord and wiring can start fires.

question: In a rooftop mechanical space with an ambient temperature of 45 degrees Celsius, a 6 AWG THHN copper conductor ends on 75 degree Celsius terminals. The load is not continuous, and the electrician has the conductor table open on the lift. What is the maximum ampacity permitted for the conductor?

options.A: 75 amperes, the unadjusted 90 degree Celsius column value with no correction
options.B: 65 amperes, because the 75 degree terminal column value is the lower limit
options.C: 53.3 amperes, applying the 75 degree factor to the 75 degree column value
options.D: 47.9 amperes, correcting the 60 degree column with the 90 degree factor

explanation: The correct answer is B (65 amperes, because the 75 degree terminal column value is the lower limit): Start from the 90 degree column: 75 amperes x 0.87 for 41 to 45 degrees Celsius = 65.25 amperes. That is above the 75 degree column value of 65 amperes, so the terminals limit the conductor to 65 amperes. Using the 90 degree value without correction gives 75 amperes, which exceeds both limits.

question: For a hospital wing, a legally required standby generator is rated 30 kilowatts at unity power factor, single phase, 240 volts. The electrician must find the minimum ampacity for the conductors from the generator terminals to the first distribution device. What is that ampacity?

options.A: 143.8 amperes, 115 percent of the 125 ampere nameplate current
options.B: 125.0 amperes, the nameplate current with no multiplier
options.C: 156.3 amperes, 125 percent of the nameplate current
options.D: 216.5 amperes, applying the square root of three to a single-phase rating

explanation: The correct answer is A (143.8 amperes, 115 percent of the 125 ampere nameplate current): Nameplate current is 30,000 / 240 = 125 amperes. Generator output conductors must carry at least 115 percent of that, so 125 x 1.15 = 143.8 amperes. The 125 percent factor belongs to continuous loads and motor conductors, and the square root of three applies only to three-phase machines.

question: Warehouse service load calculations list 100 amperes of continuous load and 100 amperes of noncontinuous load. An inspector reviewing the job before energization finds service-entrance conductors rated 200 amperes. What minimum ampacity must the service-entrance conductors have for this load?

options.A: 200 amperes, the plain sum of the continuous and noncontinuous loads at face value
options.B: 250 amperes, 125 percent of the total of both the continuous and noncontinuous loads
options.C: 125 amperes, 125 percent of only the continuous load with the other load omitted
options.D: 225 amperes, 125 percent of the continuous load plus the noncontinuous load

explanation: The correct answer is D (225 amperes, 125 percent of the continuous load plus the noncontinuous load): Service-entrance conductors must carry the noncontinuous load plus 125 percent of the continuous load: 100 + (100 x 1.25) = 225 amperes. The 200 ampere conductors fail by 25 amperes. Applying 125 percent to both loads would give 250 amperes and oversize the conductors.

question: Inside a manufacturing plant, a feeder uses 3 AWG THHN copper in one conduit with six current-carrying conductors bundled together. The ambient temperature is normal and the terminals are rated 75 degrees Celsius. The electrician must determine the allowable ampacity of the feeder conductors. What is that ampacity?

options.A: 115 amperes, the 90 degree column value with no adjustment for the bundled conductors
options.B: 100 amperes, the 75 degree terminal column with no adjustment for the bundled conductors
options.C: 80 amperes, applying the 80 percent factor to the lower 75 degree terminal column
options.D: 92 amperes, applying the 80 percent adjustment factor to the 90 degree column

explanation: The correct answer is D (92 amperes, applying the 80 percent adjustment factor to the 90 degree column): For four to six current-carrying conductors in a raceway, the adjustment factor is 80 percent. Applying it to the 90 degree column value gives 115 x 0.80 = 92 amperes, which is below the 100 ampere 75 degree terminal limit. Applying the factor to the 75 degree column would needlessly reduce the result to 80 amperes.

question: Type NM cable runs 30 feet to a metal device box that has internal cable clamps in a finished basement. The inspector asks how the cable must be secured, and there are no other boxes along the run. Which support rule applies to this installation?

options.A: Within 6 inches of the box and at intervals not exceeding 3 feet along the run
options.B: Within 8 inches of the box and at intervals not exceeding 4.5 feet along the run
options.C: Within 12 inches of the box and at intervals not exceeding 6 feet along the run
options.D: Within 12 inches of the box and at intervals not over 4.5 feet

explanation: The correct answer is D (Within 12 inches of the box and at intervals not over 4.5 feet): Type NM cable must be secured within 12 inches of each box that has cable clamps and at intervals not exceeding 4.5 feet. The 8 inch distance applies only to single-gang nonmetallic boxes without clamps. The 6 foot interval and the 3 foot interval are not part of the NM cable rules.

question: Near a new in-ground residential swimming pool, a pool contractor installs the required general-purpose receptacle. The homeowner asks how close to the pool edge the receptacle may be placed. What is the minimum distance from the inside walls of the pool?

options.A: At least 3 feet from the inside walls of the pool
options.B: At least 5 feet from the inside walls of the pool
options.C: At least 6 feet from the inside walls of the pool
options.D: At least 10 feet from the inside walls of the pool

explanation: The correct answer is C (At least 6 feet from the inside walls of the pool): Receptacles on residential property near a permanently installed pool must be at least 6 feet from the inside walls of the pool, and at least one must be 6 to 20 feet away and GFCI protected. The 3 and 5 foot values are not the receptacle spacing rule. The GFCI requirement for the receptacle in the 6 to 20 foot band is a separate rule from the spacing minimum.

question: Wired with 10 AWG copper conductors, a lighting circuit in a retail shop is protected by a 20 ampere circuit breaker. During a safety walkthrough, an auditor asks what the branch-circuit rating is for the purposes of the code. Which rating applies?

options.A: 20 amperes, set by the rating of the overcurrent device
options.B: 16 amperes, 80 percent of the breaker rating because the lighting is continuous
options.C: 30 amperes, the 10 AWG conductor ampacity read from the 60 degree Celsius column
options.D: 35 amperes, the 10 AWG conductor ampacity read from the 75 degree Celsius column

explanation: The correct answer is A (20 amperes, set by the rating of the overcurrent device): The branch-circuit rating is the rating of the overcurrent device that protects the circuit, not the conductor ampacity. A 20 ampere breaker makes this a 20 ampere circuit even though 10 AWG conductors could carry 30 or 35 amperes. The 80 percent figure is a loading limit for continuous loads on the device, so it does not change the circuit rating. This rating limits the receptacles and loads that may be connected.

question: Feeding a detached garage subpanel from a 60 ampere breaker with 6 AWG copper phase conductors in conduit, an electrician is asked by the inspector for the minimum copper equipment grounding conductor size. The distance to the garage is 80 feet. What size is the minimum?

options.A: 12 AWG copper, the size used for 20 ampere overcurrent devices
options.B: 8 AWG copper, the size used for 100 ampere overcurrent devices
options.C: 6 AWG copper, sized to match the 6 AWG phase conductors in the conduit
options.D: 10 AWG copper, from the equipment grounding table for 60 amperes

explanation: The correct answer is D (10 AWG copper, from the equipment grounding table for 60 amperes): Table 250.122 sizes the equipment grounding conductor from the rating of the overcurrent device. A 60 ampere device requires 10 AWG copper. The distance does not change that unless the phase conductors were increased for voltage drop. The 12 AWG size matches only a 20 ampere device.

question: An aircraft hangar plan note says wiring below a stated height above the hangar floor must be suitable for a hazardous classification. The hangar houses fueled aircraft, and engines are run only outdoors. The electrician checks the code for the floor classification. Which height above the floor applies?

options.A: Up to 18 inches above the hangar floor
options.B: Up to 5 feet above the floor, the extent used near aircraft engines and fuel tanks
options.C: Up to the ceiling, since the fueled aircraft make the entire hangar volume classified
options.D: Up to 36 inches above the floor, the extent used around fuel dispensing equipment

explanation: The correct answer is A (Up to 18 inches above the hangar floor): In an aircraft hangar, the area from the floor up to 18 inches is classified Class I Division 2, and wiring there must be suitable for that classification. The 5 foot dimension belongs to the zone around aircraft engines and fuel tanks, not to the general floor classification. Fueled aircraft do not classify the whole hangar volume, and other hangar rules still apply to wiring above 18 inches.

question: In a factory, a feeder supplies a single 3-phase, 480 volt load rated 50 kVA that runs continuously for eight hours each shift. The electrician must determine the minimum feeder conductor ampacity before any correction or adjustment is applied. What is that ampacity?

options.A: 60.1 amperes, the load current alone with no continuous-load factor
options.B: 75.2 amperes, which is 125 percent of the 60.1 ampere load current
options.C: 130.2 amperes, dividing kVA by line voltage and applying 125 percent
options.D: 90.2 amperes, using 150 percent of the load current

explanation: The correct answer is B (75.2 amperes, which is 125 percent of the 60.1 ampere load current): Load current is 50,000 / (1.732 x 480) = 60.1 amperes. The load is continuous, so the feeder must carry 125 percent: 60.1 x 1.25 = 75.2 amperes. Dividing by 480 without the square root of three gives 104.2 amperes, and a 150 percent factor is not used in this rule.

question: Dim lights at a farm barn prompt a check of a 120 volt branch circuit with 12 AWG copper that carries 16 amperes over 120 feet one way. Use K of 12.9 and 6,530 circular mils for 12 AWG. What is the percent voltage drop of the circuit?

options.A: 3.2 percent, using the one-way length of 120 feet instead of the round trip
options.B: 6.3 percent, from the round-trip length and 6,530 circular mils
options.C: 4.0 percent, using the 10,380 circular mils of 10 AWG instead of 6,530
options.D: 7.6 percent, reporting the 7.6 volt drop as a percentage without dividing by source voltage

explanation: The correct answer is B (6.3 percent, from the round-trip length and 6,530 circular mils): Voltage drop is 2 x 12.9 x 16 x 120 / 6,530 = 7.6 volts. Dividing by 120 volts gives 6.3 percent, well above the 3 percent informational note recommendation for branch circuits. Using only the one-way length cuts the drop in half, and 10 AWG circular mils would understate the drop.

question: Qualified persons service an industrial plant cable tray, and the supervisor asks for the smallest single-conductor cable that may be installed in a ladder-type tray. The cables, installed by the maintenance crew, will be installed in parallel groups. Which size is the minimum permitted?

options.A: 1/0 AWG, the smallest single conductor permitted in a cable tray
options.B: 2 AWG, the smallest size permitted for parallel single conductors in a raceway
options.C: 4/0 AWG, the largest size that still needs a ladder tray with 9 inch rung spacing
options.D: 250 kcmil, the smallest size permitted without a rung spacing limit in the tray

explanation: The correct answer is A (1/0 AWG, the smallest single conductor permitted in a cable tray): In industrial facilities maintained by qualified persons, single-conductor cables in a cable tray must be 1/0 AWG or larger. Sizes from 1/0 through 4/0 go in ladder tray with rungs spaced no more than 9 inches apart, so 4/0 marks the top of that range and is not the minimum. The 250 kcmil figure is where rung spacing stops being restricted, and 2 AWG is smaller than any parallel or tray single-conductor minimum.

question: Along a warehouse wall, a crew installs a long run of EMT with several outlet boxes, and the foreman, who is checking drawings for the inspection, is asked how the raceway must be supported. Which statement gives the correct support rule for the EMT?

options.A: Supports at intervals not over 10 feet, and within 3 feet of each box
options.B: Supports at intervals not over 5 feet, and within 3 feet of each box
options.C: Supports at intervals not over 10 feet, and within 12 inches of each box
options.D: Supports at intervals not over 8 feet, and within 5 feet of each box

explanation: The correct answer is A (Supports at intervals not over 10 feet, and within 3 feet of each box): EMT must be securely fastened at least every 10 feet and within 3 feet of each outlet box, junction box, device box, cabinet or fitting. Distances of 12 inches and 4.5 feet belong to the cable rules for NM cable. The 5 foot box distance is allowed only as a special exception.

question: Under the kitchen sink, a homeowner installs a garbage disposal and plans to use a cord and plug to a receptacle in the sink cabinet. The installer needs the permitted length of the cord supplied with the disposal. Which length range does the code permit?

options.A: Not less than 12 inches and not more than 24 inches
options.B: Not less than 24 inches and not more than 48 inches
options.C: Not less than 18 inches and not more than 48 inches
options.D: Not less than 18 inches and not more than 36 inches

explanation: The correct answer is D (Not less than 18 inches and not more than 36 inches): A cord-and-plug connected food waste disposer must have a cord at least 18 inches and not more than 36 inches long, and the receptacle must be accessible. The other ranges either start or end at lengths the code does not allow. The receptacle must also be accessible, so a cord outside that range fails inspection.

question: Fourteen series modules, each rated 38 volts open-circuit, form a PV string for a house, and the inverter has a maximum DC input rating. The electrician asks which value must be used to determine the maximum system voltage. Which value is used?

options.A: Added series open-circuit voltages, corrected for the coldest expected temperature
options.B: The sum of module maximum-power voltages measured at standard test conditions
options.C: The sum of open-circuit voltages at standard test conditions, with no temperature correction applied
options.D: The inverter nameplate maximum DC input voltage rating shown on its label

explanation: The correct answer is A (Added series open-circuit voltages, corrected for the coldest expected temperature): Maximum PV system voltage is the sum of the series modules' rated open-circuit voltages corrected for the lowest expected ambient temperature, because cold weather raises voltage. Voltage at maximum power is lower and not used for this limit. The inverter rating is a limit to compare against, not the value calculated.

question: Rated 50 kVA, a single-phase 240 volt transformer serves a small commercial building. The electrician, reviewing the equipment schedule for the new tenant space, needs the full-load current of the transformer secondary to compare with the service rating. What is the full-load current?

options.A: 416.7 amperes, dividing the kVA by only the 120 volt line-to-neutral value
options.B: 120.3 amperes, applying the square root of three to the 240 volt rating
options.C: 208.3 amperes, dividing kVA by the secondary line voltage
options.D: 104.2 amperes, dividing the kVA by double the real secondary voltage of 480

explanation: The correct answer is C (208.3 amperes, dividing kVA by the secondary line voltage): For a single-phase transformer, current equals kVA times 1,000 divided by the secondary voltage: 50,000 / 240 = 208.3 amperes. A three-phase factor is wrong here, and 120 or 480 volts are not the secondary voltage of this transformer. Dividing by 120 volts or 480 volts uses a voltage the transformer does not deliver.

question: Ninety feet of rooftop PVC conduit spans two equipment pads and will see a 60 degree Fahrenheit temperature change. Table 352.44 lists 2.43 inches of expansion per 100 feet for that change. The installer needs the expected length change for the 90 foot run. What is it?

options.A: 2.4 inches, using the 60 degree table value without scaling it to 90 feet
options.B: 2.7 inches, dividing 2.43 by 0.9 instead of multiplying for the shorter run
options.C: 1.8 inches, using the 50 degree row scaled to 90 feet of conduit
options.D: 2.2 inches, scaling the table value to the 90 foot length

explanation: The correct answer is D (2.2 inches, scaling the table value to the 90 foot length): Table 352.44 gives expansion per 100 feet of PVC, so a 90 foot run at the 60 degree change expands 90 divided by 100, times 2.43, which is 2.19 inches, or about 2.2 inches. Using the table value unscaled overstates the movement, and dividing by 0.9 inverts the ratio and overstates it further. The 50 degree row is for a smaller temperature change than the one given.

question: Four bends totaling 330 degrees already exist in a conduit run between two pull points in a school corridor. The installer wants to add one more bend before the next pull point. What is the largest additional bend that keeps the run within the code limit?

options.A: 90 degrees, since one more quarter bend is allowed between any two pull points
options.B: 45 degrees, representing an eighth of a turn that is common in field bending
options.C: 30 degrees, since the total of all bends between pull points is capped at 360 degrees
options.D: None, since four bends is the maximum number between pull points under the rules

explanation: The correct answer is C (30 degrees, since the total of all bends between pull points is capped at 360 degrees): The total of all bends between pull points may not exceed 360 degrees, which is the equivalent of four quarter bends. With 330 degrees already used, only 30 degrees of additional bend remains. A bend count is not the governing limit.

question: DC circuit conductors from a rooftop array pass through an attic and wall to an inverter in a garage before reaching a readily accessible disconnect. The inspector asks which wiring method the code requires inside the building. Which method is correct?

options.A: Metal raceway, Type MC cable or listed metal enclosures, per Article 690
options.B: Nonmetallic raceway containing PV wire listed for sunlight resistance
options.C: Open PV wire clipped to the rafters when covered by insulation
options.D: Type NM cable run through attic framing and wall cavities to the inverter

explanation: The correct answer is A (Metal raceway, Type MC cable or listed metal enclosures, per Article 690): PV circuit conductors that run inside a building before the first readily accessible disconnect must be in metal raceways, Type MC cable or metal enclosures. Nonmetallic raceways, open PV wire and Type NM cable do not meet this requirement for those conductors. The inspector checks this at the point where conductors leave the array until the disconnect.

question: Type I construction governs a new 600-seat theater, and the electrician needs a wiring method for exposed branch circuits above the ceiling. Several options are considered under the assembly occupancy rules. Which method may be used in this exposed location?

options.A: Type NM-B cable, since the theater circuits operate at only 120 volts
options.B: Rigid PVC conduit installed exposed above the ceiling and supported on trapeze hangers
options.C: Type MC cable, a metal-sheathed method suited to this construction type
options.D: Electrical nonmetallic tubing run exposed above the ceiling with no encasement or barrier

explanation: The correct answer is C (Type MC cable, a metal-sheathed method suited to this construction type): In assembly occupancies of Type I or II construction, wiring must be in metal raceways, Type MC cable or AC cable. Nonmetallic raceways are allowed only when encased in at least 2 inches of concrete. Type NM cable and exposed nonmetallic raceway do not qualify here.

question: Planning to use a 20 ampere, 120 volt general-use snap switch on a small shop exhaust fan motor, a customer asks the supply house clerk how large a motor load the switch may control. The clerk must state the largest motor current. What is that limit?

options.A: 16 amperes, found as 80 percent of the 20 ampere switch rating
options.B: 20 amperes, the full ampere rating printed on the switch
options.C: 12 amperes, which is 60 percent of the switch ampere rating
options.D: 10 amperes, which is 50 percent of the switch ampere rating

explanation: The correct answer is A (16 amperes, found as 80 percent of the 20 ampere switch rating): A general-use snap switch may control a motor load up to 80 percent of the switch ampere rating at its rated voltage. For a 20 ampere switch that is 16 amperes. The full rating applies to resistive loads, not motors.

question: Stockroom inspection at a retail store reveals a 14 AWG copper branch circuit protected by a 20 ampere breaker. The conductor insulation is rated 90 degrees Celsius, and its table value is 25 amperes. What correction does the inspector require?

options.A: Accept the circuit because 14 AWG THHN has a 90 degree ampacity of 25 amperes
options.B: Replace the breaker with a 30 ampere breaker rated for the 90 degree column
options.C: Reduce the overcurrent device to 15 amperes or install 12 AWG conductors
options.D: Add GFCI protection to offset the undersized conductor

explanation: The correct answer is C (Reduce the overcurrent device to 15 amperes or install 12 AWG conductors): Small conductor rules limit 14 AWG copper to a 15 ampere overcurrent device, no matter how high the insulation temperature rating is. The fix is to lower the device to 15 amperes or to install 12 AWG conductors. A 25 ampere table value does not permit a 20 ampere breaker.

question: Located 180 feet from the main panel, a new detached workshop prompts the electrician to look up the code guidance on voltage drop for the feeder and branch circuits combined. What guidance does the informational note give for maximum voltage drop?

options.A: 2 percent on the branch circuit and 3 percent on feeder and branch combined
options.B: 5 percent on the branch circuit and 8 percent on feeder and branch combined
options.C: 3 percent on the branch circuit and 5 percent on feeder and branch combined
options.D: 3 percent on feeder and branch combined and 5 percent on the branch alone

explanation: The correct answer is C (3 percent on the branch circuit and 5 percent on feeder and branch combined): The informational notes recommend a maximum voltage drop of 3 percent on the branch circuit and 5 percent on the feeder and branch circuit combined. They are recommendations for efficient operation, not enforceable requirements. The 3 percent figure targets the branch circuit alone, while the 5 percent figure covers the total from service to outlet.

question: Passing over a dwelling roof with a slope of 6 inches of rise per 12 inches of run, a 120/240 volt service drop is checked by the inspector. The roof overhang is wide and the drop passes well beyond the eave. What is the minimum clearance above the roof surface?

options.A: 8 feet above the roof surface, the flat roof clearance value
options.B: 3 feet above the roof surface, the reduced value for a slope of 4 in 12
options.C: 18 inches above the roof surface, the short overhang value
options.D: 12 feet above the roof surface, the residential ground value

explanation: The correct answer is B (3 feet above the roof surface, the reduced value for a slope of 4 in 12): Service drop conductors must clear a roof by 8 feet, but where the slope is at least 4 inches of rise per 12 inches of run the clearance may be reduced to 3 feet. The 18 inch value applies only to a limited overhang of the drop that has a restricted length. A wide overhang does not change the 3 foot value, which depends on the roof slope.

question: Output from a 7.6 kW single-phase inverter operating at 240 volts feeds the utility interactive PV circuit. During a rooftop solar retrofit, the electrician must select the minimum overcurrent device, and the inverter output is a continuous load. Which standard size should be selected?

options.A: 40 amperes, the next standard size above 125 percent of the 31.7 amperes
options.B: 35 amperes, using only 110 percent of the inverter output current
options.C: 30 amperes, the standard size just below the inverter output current
options.D: 50 amperes, applying 125 percent twice before rounding to a standard size

explanation: The correct answer is A (40 amperes, the next standard size above 125 percent of the 31.7 amperes): Output current is 7,600 / 240 = 31.7 amperes. Inverter output circuits need an overcurrent device rated at least 125 percent of that, which is 39.6 amperes, so the next standard size is 40 amperes. A 30 ampere device is below the output current and a 50 ampere device oversizes the circuit.

question: Box trucks use the delivery driveway of a small warehouse every day, and a utility installs a new 120/240 volt service drop that crosses it. The drop also passes over a landscaped garden strip. What is the minimum clearance over the driveway?

options.A: 10 feet above the driveway, the building entrance value
options.B: 12 feet above the driveway, the residential driveway value
options.C: 18 feet above the driveway, the truck traffic area value
options.D: 15 feet above the driveway, the over 300 volt value

explanation: The correct answer is C (18 feet above the driveway, the truck traffic area value): Over driveways on other than residential property and areas subject to truck traffic, the clearance for a service drop is 18 feet. The 12 foot figure applies to residential driveways without truck traffic. The garden strip does not govern, because the driveway is the most restrictive crossing.

question: Nameplate current on a 5 horsepower, 230 volt single-phase motor reads 29.2 amperes, while the motor table full-load current is 28 amperes. The electrician, working from the motor tables, must size the branch-circuit conductors. What is the minimum conductor ampacity?

options.A: 28 amperes, the table full-load current used with no 125 percent multiplier
options.B: 35 amperes, which is 125 percent of the 28 ampere motor table full-load value, per 430.22
options.C: 36.5 amperes, 125 percent of the nameplate current instead of the table current
options.D: 29.2 amperes, the nameplate current used with no 125 percent multiplier

explanation: The correct answer is B (35 amperes, which is 125 percent of the 28 ampere motor table full-load value, per 430.22): Motor branch-circuit conductors are sized at 125 percent of the table full-load current, not the nameplate current. That gives 28 x 1.25 = 35 amperes. The nameplate current is used only for overload protection.

question: Exposed EMT along a loading dock will carry six 8 AWG THHN conductors, each with a cross-sectional area of 0.0366 square inch. Forty percent of the area is 0.213 square inch for 3/4 inch trade size and 0.346 square inch for 1 inch. Which is the smallest trade size?

options.A: 3/4 inch, with 0.213 square inch available at 40 percent fill
options.B: 1/2 inch, with room for six small conductors at 40 percent fill
options.C: 1 1/4 inch, matching the next larger standard trade size
options.D: 1 inch, with 0.346 square inch available at 40 percent fill

explanation: The correct answer is D (1 inch, with 0.346 square inch available at 40 percent fill): The conductors total 6 x 0.0366 = 0.2196 square inch. The 3/4 inch EMT allows only 0.213 square inch at 40 percent fill, so it is too small. The 1 inch EMT allows 0.346 square inch and is the smallest size that works.

question: Powering the house from a portable generator through an inlet connected to the panelboard is the homeowner's plan, and the generator nameplate shows 80 amperes. The electrician must identify, before any wiring starts, what the installation requires. Which item does the code require?

options.A: A ground-fault circuit interrupter on the generator inlet receptacle and cord set
options.B: Transfer equipment that blocks interconnection with the utility supply
options.C: A bonding jumper between the generator neutral and the service neutral bar
options.D: A permanent sign stating the generator wattage placed near the utility meter

explanation: The correct answer is B (Transfer equipment that blocks interconnection with the utility supply): A generator that supplies premises wiring needs transfer equipment, such as a transfer switch or listed interlock, that prevents the generator and utility supplies from being connected together. Without it, the generator could backfeed the utility lines and endanger line workers. Listed transfer switches and interlock kits are the usual ways to meet this rule.

question: Installing a 20 horsepower motor and its controller in a mechanical room, a maintenance contractor is asked by the inspector where the motor controller disconnecting means must be located. The motor is on a different floor than the controller. Which location satisfies the code?

options.A: Within sight of the controller location, visible from the enclosure
options.B: Within sight of the motor only, since the motor is the final load served
options.C: Anywhere in the same building if the disconnect is clearly labeled for the motor
options.D: At the service equipment, since it is the source of supply for the building

explanation: The correct answer is A (Within sight of the controller location, visible from the enclosure): A motor controller disconnecting means must be located in sight of the controller location, where within sight means visible and not more than 50 feet away. The motor location has its own rule, and labeling alone does not make a remote disconnect acceptable. The controller disconnect lets a worker open the circuit at the equipment being serviced.

question: Calculated ampacity of 95 amperes applies to a feeder conductor that supplies an 80 ampere noncontinuous load in a small factory. The electrician wants the largest overcurrent device the rules allow for this feeder. What is the maximum device rating?

options.A: 90 amperes, the standard size just below the conductor ampacity value
options.B: 100 amperes, the next standard size above the conductor ampacity
options.C: 125 amperes, rounding up 125 percent of the conductor ampacity value
options.D: 80 amperes, the noncontinuous load itself used as the maximum rating

explanation: The correct answer is B (100 amperes, the next standard size above the conductor ampacity): When the ampacity does not match a standard device size, the next higher standard size is permitted if it does not exceed 800 amperes. For 95 amperes that is 100 amperes. Rounding down is allowed but is not the maximum, and 125 amperes is above the permitted next size.

question: Several fixed appliances are installed in a kitchen remodel, and the inspector asks which rating threshold requires an appliance disconnecting means. The appliances are permanently connected, with a mix of ratings from a small ventilation fan up to a large wall oven. At what rating does the disconnect requirement start?

options.A: Rated above 300 volt-amperes or above one-eighth horsepower
options.B: Rated above 300 volt-amperes or above one-third horsepower, borrowed from the cord-and-plug controller rule
options.C: Rated above 600 volt-amperes or above one-eighth horsepower, doubling the apparent power limit only
options.D: Rated above 300 volt-amperes or above one horsepower, raising only the motor-rated limit

explanation: The correct answer is A (Rated above 300 volt-amperes or above one-eighth horsepower): A permanently connected appliance rated above 300 volt-amperes or one-eighth horsepower needs a disconnecting means, and the branch-circuit breaker may serve if it is within sight or lockable.
